finding.title: Messages over 65535 bytes pass the size check, but their length is silently truncated to u16, so the stream is corrupted

other.title: No test round-trips a message at MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES or just above u16::MAX

findings.title: Messages over 65535 bytes pass the size check, but their length is silently truncated to u16, so the stream is corrupted
findings.scenario: MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES is 256*1024, and the doc comment says uploads are split into chunks of that size. A 262144-byte chunk passes the `> MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES` check. `262144 as u16` is 0, so the header says 0 and all 262144 payload bytes follow. decode returns an empty message and then reads the payload's first two bytes as the next frame's header. Every message from 65536 to 262144 bytes gets a wrong length, and the stream loses sync with no error.
findings.whyNotPrevented: `as u16` truncates without warning. The limit lives in src/limits.rs and was not lowered. The tests only cover 5-byte messages, plus MAX+1, which is rejected before the cast.
findings.measuredBy: Grep "MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES": src/limits.rs:2 `pub const MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES: usize = 256 * 1024;` (> u16::MAX 65535)

findings.title: Length over 65535 is silently truncated by the u16 cast, which corrupts the stream
findings.scenario: A message of 70000 bytes is under MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES (256*1024), so encode accepts it. The header records 70000 mod 65536 = 4464, and all 70000 bytes go out after it. decode returns a 4464-byte message and then reads the leftover payload bytes as the next frame's header. Upload chunks are exactly 262144 bytes, so every one gets the header 0 (262144 mod 65536): an empty message, with the real payload read as later garbage frames.
findings.whyNotPrevented: The guard still checks against MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES = 256*1024 in src/limits.rs:2, which is larger than u16::MAX. `as u16` truncates without warning. The tests only use 5-byte messages and one message of MAX+1 that is rejected, so no test covers lengths from 65536 to MAX.

findings.title: Messages from 65,536 bytes up to MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES (256 KiB) get a wrong u16 length and corrupt the stream
findings.scenario: The size check still allows messages up to 256 KiB (262,144 bytes), but a 2-byte header can only hold lengths up to 65,535. Upload chunks are MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES long (limits.rs comment). Take a 70,000-byte chunk: it passes the check, `as u16` cuts its length to 4,464, and the full 70,000 bytes are still written. decode then returns the first 4,464 bytes as the message and reads the rest of the payload as the next frame headers. findings.title: Off-by-one: the last window leaves out the newest reading, and exactly five readings give no average
findings.scenario: With readings [20,20,20,20,20,40,40,40,40,40], the last window is values[4..9]. It skips the newest 40 and averages to 36. The intended average of the last five is 40. findings.scenario: send_weekly passes project.watchers(). If watchers() returns a list the project keeps internally, every weekly run adds TEAM_INBOX to the project's real watcher list. Each run then sends one more team-inbox copy, and the inbox shows up as a watcher. Callers that pass one shared list to several build_digest calls hit the same buildup.
findings.whyNotPrevented: No Project.watchers implementation could be found in the repository to show it returns a copy, and no test checks that the caller's list is unchanged after the call.
findings.measuredBy: Grep "watchers" in repo: only the call site in weekly.py

findings.title: No test calls the default path twice or checks that the caller's list stays unchanged
findings.scenario: The new test passes a list literal once, so it cannot catch the shared-default buildup or the in-place change. Neither is covered for send_weekly either.
